newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher, H&M recovers, Volvo up.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher, H&M recovers, Volvo up.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Friday, cheered by favourable U.S. trends.
The Stockholm bourse's general index rises 0.93 percent to 2,869.01 in turnover totalling 5.31 billion crowns.
"There has probably been a lot of trading. It doesn't feel as if there are lots of customer orders at the moment," a broker said.

Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz jumped 11.5 crowns to 246 in a rebound after plunging 19.5 crowns a day earlier when it announced it would transfer its shares from the main A list to the smaller O list for tax reasons.
"The question you can ask yourself is how much of today's upturn was short-covering," a trader said.
Automotive group Volvo fell four crowns to 206.5, building on its day earlier five crown fall as the period for determining the share price of its redemption program ended.
Telecoms group Ericsson rose 4.5 crowns to 286.

"Ericsson broke a technical resistance level at 280-284 crowns and since then everyone who has looked at the share from a technical point of view has had a big buy on it up to at least 300 crowns," a trader said, adding: "I think Ericsson and the bourse will keep rising next week."
The bank and construction sectors were going strong, up 1.32 percent and 1.98 percent, respectively.
Swedbank jumped 7.5 crowns to 164 and Handelsbanken rose 3.5 crowns to 224.5.
Dealers said those two had been lagging behind rivals S-E-Banken and Nordbanken which have been rising on previous merger rumours but ended flat on Friday.
Drugs major Astra rose 1.5 crowns to 129.5.
